# The spine in the class system — the plan, as a list (compressed)

*Generated by `tools/modular_spine_plan.py`. The numbers are read from `curriculum_spine.json`, `modular_signatures.json`, `void_spawnlists.json`, `rooms.json` and `artifact_roles.json`; the proposed families are authored in the script and are proposals until someone saves them in the studio. Palle, 23 Oct 2026: "make a plan to integrate all the spine in a list" … "fold the compressed version into the plan."*

The grammar has **51 terms** today, almost all of them the primitives sequence. The spine has **25 sequences, 209 maps, 1602 placed artifacts, 205 Void floors**. The plan proposes **52 families (108 variants through their axes)** in the spine's own **seven phase chapters**, and names the **six pieces the kernel must grow** to build them. A family is one term with a `dna.axes` declaration, so the registry's sweep, gallery and bite critic apply to every variant for free. Every family is built from terms that exist, so the derivation order stays a tutorial path. Nothing on a floor is rebuilt; the order is Palle's.

## What was compressed

- twelve engines → **two** (`by`: a function of index and time per part; `step`: a rule per part from its neighbours), with the rule names kept for the lessons;
- `vary` → the same `by` at t = 0; array, times, recurse, rewrite → **one `replicate`** with four presets;
- the shader axis → a key on `associate` (the ink stroke already proves it), not a kernel piece;
- boolean and isosurface → **one `field`** (a solid from a function of space), to be checked against the boolean halls;
- 82 terms → **52 families**; 17 new chapters → the **7 spine phases**; 6 waves → **4**; `connect` moved to wave 1 because a spring is a connect with a rule;
- the done gate: not the scanner (it matches primitive sets and will never read a flock as swarm) but **every floor's primary has a twin** — a finite target;
- one verlet in both renderers, Jolt only for the rigid fall that exists — a second implementation of one rule drifts (the long-museum lesson).

## The loop — what one sequence goes through

1. **scan** — `python tools/modular_scan.py` reads the sequence's artifacts into primitives, parts, behaviour, interaction (a hypothesis, coarse by design)
2. **name** — author the row's families in `/modular-studio` (expression, parents, build JSON, Save to terms.json); each is a gate: the construction plays, the scaffold goes, the thing stands alone; the axis goes on the mod_ token as `dna.axes`, DERIVED from the build, never typed
3. **grow** — if the row needs a kernel piece, add it to `builder.gd` AND `modular-terms.ts` in the same change, with a family that uses it, so the two renderers cannot drift
4. **prove** — `probe_modular.gd` (every term builds, no body without a collider, no busy-parent warnings), `check_compile.gd`, `tsc` on the modular files, `check_dna_declarations.py` on the new axes
5. **register** — `python tools/build_modular_registry.py` (mod_<term> tokens), `capture_multi_angle` per token (windowed; headless saves nothing), `build_dna_gallery.py` per family, `sync_artifact_captures.py`, `build_void_spawnlists.py`
6. **twin** — stand the family's mod_ token beside the floor's primary through the bridge (`live_update_spawn_test.py --via-bridge --token mod_<term>`); rooms.json is the one model; a map gets it only where the hall is map-authored
7. **path** — `python tools/modular_path.py` regenerates MODULAR_PATH.md; the lesson now has rooms to stand in
8. **walk** — the headset (APK export) or `--vr-link` desktop; the hand message names what arrived

## The order — four waves, by what the kernel needs

- **wave 1** — `connect`, `by`, `measure`, `step` with its first rule (spring) — fourteen sequences build on the kernel as it is plus these: 1·primitives, 2·transformation, 3·array_tutorial, 4·color, 5·tiling, 6·change, 7·forces, 8·formfinding, 9·wavefunctions, 10·randomness, 11·noise, 12·shaders, 16·proceduralgeneration, 21·graphtheory
- **wave 2** — `replicate` — the self-containing terms: 14·fractals, 15·lsystems
- **wave 3** — the remaining `step` rules (ca, verlet, boids, learn) and `field`: 13·cellularautomata, 17·softbodies, 18·isosurfaces, 19·boolean_surfaces, 20·swarmintelligence, 22·machinelearning
- **wave 4** — synthesis — no new construction: compare the grammar, turn its parameters, rewrite it: 23·foundationscrisis, 24·qfeplaboratory, 25·postfoundationscrisis

## The kernel work list — six pieces, each named once

- **connect** — a relation between two NAMED parts of one compose — drawn as a line it is an edge, with a step rule it is a spring, with a number it is a weight. `{"op":"connect","a":"n1","b":"n2"}`. Both builders. First, because forces (7) needs it long before graph theory (21) names it. Used by: forces, formfinding, graphtheory, machinelearning.
- **by** — the parameter function f(index, t): `{"by":{"fn":"list|sine|noise|random|lerp", …}}` — on an array it is `vary` (t = 0: colour, height, rotation, phase per part); on an engine it is motion (the same function with t running). One implementation serves both. Used by: transformation, color, tiling, change, wavefunctions, randomness, noise, proceduralgeneration, qfeplaboratory.
- **replicate** — one replication operator with four presets — array (X → X X X X shifted), times, recurse (X → n transformed copies of X, bounded `depth`: the only place self-containment is allowed) and rewrite (a string rule, generations; the turtle is its interpreter). Used by: fractals, lsystems, foundationscrisis, postfoundationscrisis.
- **step** — the neighbourhood engine: a named rule applied per part from its neighbours and connects — spring, field, boids, ca, verlet, learn share one interface. ONE verlet in both renderers (SoftBody3D cannot squeeze; Jolt only for the rigid fall that exists), so the two sides cannot drift. Used by: forces, formfinding, cellularautomata, softbodies, swarmintelligence, machinelearning, qfeplaboratory.
- **field** — a solid from a function of space: a scalar field over a grid → marching cubes (iso); union / subtract / intersect as min / max of distance fields (boolean) — to be checked against the boolean_surfaces halls before the CSG nodes are dropped. Used by: isosurfaces, boolean_surfaces.
- **measure** — the instrument half of the grammar (Palle, 23 Oct: "add measure as the sixth piece"): a value READ off a thing — a length, a count, an entropy, a projection, a loss — `{"op":"measure","of":{…},"what":"length|count|entropy|…"}`; RETAINED across steps as a record, a trail, a history (the sibling of `trace_data`, which carries what a visitor meant); and COMPARED with another under a stated rule (`{"op":"compare","a":…,"b":…,"rule":…}`). It is what the spine's principles mostly say — compare (104), measure (67), retain (45) of the 420 — and no construction says it. Shown as a label, a bar or a readout beside the thing it reads; both builders. Used by: primitives, forces, wavefunctions, randomness, cellularautomata, isosurfaces, machinelearning, qfeplaboratory.

## The edges of the kernel — and where the leaks go

Every rule refuses something (`doc/EDGE_INVENTORY.md`: thirteen material kinds), and what it refuses is a **leak**: kept on the `LeakData` bus, named, never counted. A kernel piece is a rule, so each has edges by construction — its parameters. They are declared here so a family inherits them in the open instead of shipping a silent ceiling (the Cantor set's fourth removal is a `replicate` edge). The scaffold is a leak too: what a construction removes when it is done, the line inside the tape — `composite.gd` spills it before freeing it. The conceptual edges A–M (`doc/EDGES_OF_ALGORITHM.md`) are not kernel pieces; they are what the late-spine families are *about*, and the plan reads φ·dE as their political term: what F leaves out accumulates over t, and the leak bus is where it accumulates.

| piece | edge kind | parameter | what escapes | leak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| connect | coupling | the relation itself | the two parts' right to differ — a spring pulls them alike; the difference it removes each tick is the leak | spill: the displacement a spring undid |
| by | quantiser | index | everything between two parts: f is sampled at integers, the curve between them is never built | spill: the curve between the samples, as points |
| by | order | seed | every other sequence the seed did not choose | no spill — nothing was computed |
| replicate | ceiling | depth / n | the copies past the bound — MAX_DEPTH 24 in builder.gd; the Cantor set's fourth removal (EDGE_INVENTORY: deadband at 0.01 m) | spill: the transforms of the copies not built |
| replicate | deadband | min size | a copy smaller than the floor — the level at which a fractal stops being a picture of itself | spill: the sub-floor copies, as points |
| step | clock | tick | what happens between two ticks — the rule refuses on its own time | no spill |
| step | ball | radius | every neighbour outside the radius (boids, verlet): one region, every arrival alike | spill: the neighbours a part did not see |
| step | shelf | clamp | the stiffness, speed or force past the clamp | spill: the force removed |
| measure | quantiser | resolution | everything finer than the instrument reads — a length to the millimetre, an entropy to two decimals; the thing has more than the reading | spill: the residual, as a number the bus does not rank |
| measure | window | record length | what the record forgets — a trail keeps the last N, a history the last T; the earlier passage is gone from the end you are not watching | spill: the dropped entries |
| measure | coupling | comparison rule | what the rule equates — two things compared as lengths lose the right to differ in everything but length | no spill — the rule is named, which is the whole lesson |
| field | deadband | iso threshold | every value under the threshold — the field exists there and no surface is drawn | spill: the sub-threshold cells |
| field | mask | subtract | the subtracted volume — a body that is never seen; boolean's remainder is the clearest leak in the kernel | spill: the subtracted volume, as points |
| field | quantiser | grid | the surface between grid cells (marching cubes interpolates, it does not know) | no spill |

14 declared edges on six pieces; 6 families inherit a named material edge from the artifact they twin: `fractal` (fractals), `scalar_field` (isosurfaces), `boolean_pair` (boolean_surfaces), `crisis_table` (foundationscrisis), `self_member` (foundationscrisis), `axis_sweep` (qfeplaboratory). A twin that hides the edge its original shows is a lie twin; the gate is that it spills what the original dropped.

## The floors — what each Void floor becomes

205 floors in `commons/void/rooms.json`, 1449 artifacts: **189 twins** (one reconstruction per floor, beside the primary), **53 swap candidates** (already a small term; Palle's call per floor), **213 documents** (films, plaques, screens, sliders — never a construction), **994 kept** as they are. No floor is rebuilt; walls, route and props stay. Drawn at `/modular-plan`; stood up in three.js at `/modular-plan/3d`. 4 of the floors carry the book's own edge sentence (the dependency the hall cannot absorb, `edge` on its pearl in `commons/data/book/*.json`) — the rest of that corpus is keyed to the museum's chambers, not to Void floors, so it does not reach them here.

## Done looks like

- every spine sequence has its families saved from the studio under its phase chapter, each a gate that plays and ends with the intended thing alone, each axis declared from the build and passing the declaration gate;
- `probe_modular` builds every term; the registry has a `mod_` token, a capture and a DNA gallery per family;
- **every floor's primary has a twin beside it** (189 floors), placed through the bridge and seen on the headset; swaps only where Palle marked them;
- `MODULAR_PATH.md` reads as the tutorial: seven phase chapters in spine order, every lesson built from lessons before it, with rooms to stand in;
- the synthesis floors hold the three meta-terms: the grammar compared, parametrized, rewritten.
